subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to diagnostics for dropped Telegram `MEDIA:` directives while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns root expansion, or should it define the host-local media root policy itself?
rationale: The diagnostics fix is narrow, but accepting more host-local paths changes a security-sensitive file-read/upload boundary and overlaps an open broader root-policy proposal.

options.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots Elsewhere
options.body: Keep this issue focused on reasoned dropped-media logging and user-visible notices, while the root expansion contract stays with the canonical media-root policy work.

options.title: Define Root Policy Here
options.body: Use this issue to specify and implement the permanent host-local MEDIA root contract across schema, docs, runtime, and tests.

options.title: Document Current Boundary Only
options.body: Decline new root expansion and close the remaining behavior after improving docs and diagnostics around managed roots and file-read policy.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots Elsewhere
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on reasoned dropped-media logging and user-visible notices, while the root expansion contract stays with the canonical media-root policy work.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest recent history on outbound media access and root-policy plumbing.
